case_name: Balvinder Singh Alias Bablu vs Smt. Neha Nangla
facts_of_case: Petitioner-husband seeking to assail an order granting maintenance pendente lite and litigation expenses in favour of the respondent-wife under section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955.

legal_principles.principle: Remedy of appeal is provided under section 28(1) for all decrees made by the court in any proceeding under the Hindu Marriage Act.
legal_principles.held: A perusal of section 28 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 would show that remedy of appeal is provided under section 28(1) in terms whereof all decrees made by the Court in any proceeding under the said Act are appealable as decrees of the court made in exercise of its original civil jurisdiction.

legal_principles.principle: Orders passed under section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act are not appealable.
legal_principles.held: Section 28(2) provides the orders against which remedy of appeal is available to an aggrieved party to a matrimonial litigation. Section 28(2) makes orders passed under section 25 or section 26 appealable. Thus, there is an express exclusion of orders passed under section 24 of the Hindu Marriage Act, 1955 in terms whereof an interim maintenance and litigation expenses come to be awarded in favour of a spouse.

outcome.final_order: The appeal is not appealable one and is accordingly dismissed. The amount deposited by the appellant shall be allowed to be withdrawn.
